detail.text: The air is wrong here, too still, too watchful.
Old offerings rot in a niche, some barely cold.
Frost rimes every surface though the season forbids it.
The mud holds footprints that lead only inward.
A faint sigil-hum rises as you step closer.
Ash sifts down from a sky with no cloud.
Whatever happened here happened quickly, and then stopped.
Someone tidied this place, which is somehow worse.
Everything portable is gone. Everything heavy remains.
The ground is packed hard, as if from long standing.
There is no sound at all, not even insects.
A tally is scratched into the stone and never finished.
The canopy closes overhead and the light goes green and slow.
The grain lies flattened in a shape too regular for wind.
Someone has swept the threshold clean and left no other trace.
Stones clatter down the slope long after you have stopped moving.
The water runs clear over something pale on the bottom.
Heat-shimmer makes the middle distance untrustworthy.
Wind has scoured the ground down to grit and old iron.
Your breath hangs in front of you and does not drift.
The rock is warm enough through your boots to count as a warning.
Your rings and buckles pull gently toward a spot with nothing in it.
The ruts are fresh, and the traffic went one way only.
Reeds have been cut back from the water in a careful arc.
The grain is unharvested and perfectly kept. Someone is paying for that.
Every fence-line here has been moved at least once, and recently.
The mud has been churned by so many boots it has stopped being mud.
Both armies' colours rot in the same ditch, at the same rate.
Nothing here has fallen over. That is the first thing wrong with it.
The wind has blown one direction so long the ground has taken its shape.
Everything here carries somebody's mark, including the ground.
The noise of the works carries for miles and never entirely stops.
The bones point the same way the road does.
Salt has crept up the walls and eaten the lower third of everything.
The road ended some way back and nobody marked where.
The forest has taken the walls and left the doorways.
The ice is old enough to be a different colour and clear enough to regret.
Cloud forms below you and hides the way back down.
The water table here is mostly people.
Every name on the stone was cut by a different hand.
The green here has weight, and it leans.
Nothing that lives here has learned to be afraid of you.
They built here on purpose. The evidence of how that went is underfoot.
The glass holds the shape of the moment it cooled.
The books are intact, which after this long is not reassuring.
The catalogue is still legible, and still being kept.
The seasons here disagree with one another across a hundred paces.
Every faction's mark is on this stone, each struck through by the next.
Every ridgeline here has a sightline onto this one.
The path is good, well-kept, and used by people who did not build it.
The chart is wrong. The chart is always wrong here, twice a day.
Everything on this beach came off a different ship.
You have not seen the sky in some time and cannot say how long.
These trees were old before the Collapse and were not impressed by it.

complication.text: Something watches from just past the light.
A cold thread of dread says not everything here is dead.
Fresh tracks say you are not the first here today.
A resonance that matches no known ley-line pulls at your teeth.
You have the distinct sense of having been expected.
One of your party is already walking toward it, and cannot say why.
The quiet has the quality of held breath.
Whatever left these marks has not gone far.
There is a second set of your own bootprints, going the other way.
Nothing here is dangerous. That is the part you dislike.
The stones hold a shape your eye keeps trying to complete.
The water settles wrong, as though something under it just stopped moving.
The cold here has a direction, and the direction is you.
The ground ticks as it cools, and the rhythm is too even.
The birds went silent before you arrived, not after.
Your own tracks behind you are already gone.
Something up the slope shifts its footing and holds still again.
A levy's charm-oath still hangs in the air, looking for a throat to settle in.
Two families claim this ground, and both are waiting to see which of them you insult.
The river runs a brown it did not get from soil.
Scavengers stop working long enough to count how many of you there are.
Something in the ice has changed position since you last looked at it.
The cold is going out of the air, which here is not a mercy.
Two charters cover this ground and neither will admit the other exists.
Something mechanical has been watching the road, and it keeps a ledger.
A town stands clear on the horizon. It has been the same distance away for an hour.
Someone has been drinking here recently. The well is dry.
The wood is paying attention, the way a room does when you enter it.
Something large came through here at speed and did not slow for obstacles.
The silhouette in the ice was facing the other way this morning.
The thaw line has moved up the slope since you started climbing.
The dead here are not restless. They are organised.
Someone has left fresh flowers, and there is nobody within a day's walk.
The tide is going out considerably faster than tides do.
Something in the canopy is keeping pace with you and not hiding it.
The ground is warmer than it was a hundred paces back, and still warming.
The vents have gone quiet. All of them. At once.
The wards are holding. You would rather know what they are holding in.
The water is lower than it was an hour ago, and nothing is draining.
The ley-lines run close enough here to feel in your fillings.
Everyone who has held this ground lost it. You are aware of the pattern.
You are being watched from high ground, competently.
The cache was full yesterday. Somebody is running ahead of you.
The tide is coming in behind you, across ground it did not cover this morning.
Something came ashore with the last storm and has not gone back.
The wood has an opinion about you, and it is still forming.
The storm-track is fresh, and the ground inside it is different ground.

weather.text: The light is going, and going faster than the hour allows.
A wind gets up out of nowhere and dies just as fast.
Cloud comes over and the temperature drops a full season.
The sky has the flat white look that comes before something.
Snow starts, fine as flour, and does not stop.
The wind carries ice fine enough to breathe.
The sun stands directly overhead and refuses to move.
A dust haze blanks the horizon in every direction.
Ash sifts down warm and settles on your shoulders.
Heat rises off the ground in visible sheets.
Rain arrives in the canopy long before it reaches you.
Fog stands between the trunks in vertical columns.
Mist comes off the water in long slow ropes.
The sky above this spot is a slightly different colour than the sky beside it.
Cloud pours over the ridge and swallows the way you came.
The whole field moves at once, though the air is still.
The low gold light makes the downs look settled, which they are not.
Rain fills the shell-scars and turns the field into a hundred small brown mirrors.
The white runs on until it stops being distance and becomes absence.
Smoke lies along the valley in flat grey strata, one for each working day.
The heat comes off the pan as a solid wall you have to walk into.
Rain finds its way through the canopy in cold single drops, hours apart.
The air is thin enough that your own heartbeat is the loudest thing on the mountain.
The mist never lifts here. It only changes height.
The storm is not on the horizon. It is directly overhead, and has not started.
The sky over the plateau is the colour of a healing bruise.
The air down here tastes of wet paper and deep standing water.
Four weathers meet over the Convergence and none of them wins.
Cloud fills the valleys and turns the crags into islands.
The surge comes up the strand faster than a walk and slower than a run.
An elemental front is coming up from the west and the canopy has already gone quiet.
